source.book: Tajweed Rules of the Qur'an — Part One

prerequisites: Recognize the Arabic letter noon: ن.
Recognize fathah, kasrah, dammah, and sukoon.
learningOutcomes: Define noon saakinah and recognize نْ.
Define tanween as an extra noon sound heard when continuing.
Explain two differences between noon saakinah and tanween.
Use the routine: find the target, then inspect the next letter.

linguistic.ar: السكون هو عدم الحركة، والتنوين هو التصويت بالنون.
linguistic.en: Sukoon indicates no vowel; tanween produces an additional noon sound.

technical.ar: النون الساكنة هي نون أصلية خالية من الحركة، تثبت لفظًا وخطًا ووصلاً ووقفًا. والتنوين نون ساكنة زائدة تلحق آخر الاسم لفظًا لا خطًا، وتثبت في الوصل دون الوقف.
technical.en: Noon saakinah is an original noon with no vowel, written and pronounced. Tanween is an additional noon sound at the end of a noun when continuing; it is heard but not written as the letter noon.

studentFriendly.ar: إذا رأيت نْ فهذه نون ساكنة مكتوبة. وإذا رأيت ً أو ٍ أو ٌ فستسمع صوت نون عند الوصل، وهذا هو التنوين.
studentFriendly.en: If you see نْ, it is a written noon saakinah. If you see ً, ٍ, or ٌ, you hear a noon sound when continuing; that is tanween.

definition.memoryFormula: نْ = نون مكتوبة ساكنة  |  ً ٍ ٌ = صوت نون زائد عند الوصل

keyTerms.en: an extra noon sound at the end of a noun when continuing

teacherPreparation: Display the forms one at a time: نْ, ـًـ, ـٍـ, ـٌـ.
Say each form before asking the learner to name it.
Keep this lesson focused on recognition before introducing the four rules.
Contrast what is seen in writing with what is heard during continuation.

openingReview.teacherPrompt: Show نَ، نِ، نُ، نْ and ask which noon has no vowel.
Review fathah, kasrah, dammah, and sukoon.

conceptExplanation.text: Every coming rule begins with the same first step: find noon saakinah or tanween, then look at the immediately following letter.
Build visual and auditory recognition before naming izhar, idgham, iqlab, or ikhfa'.

lessonPath.title: See
lessonPath.text: Compare نْ with the three tanween signs.

lessonPath.title: Hear
lessonPath.text: Notice the noon sound during continuation.

lessonPath.title: Locate
lessonPath.text: Find the target before the next letter.

visualExplanation.display: نْ  ≠  ً ٍ ٌ   |   كلاهما يعطينا صوت نون ساكنة عند الوصل
visualExplanation.teacherUse: Ask what differs visually and what is similar in sound.

ruleSummary.condition: First locate noon saakinah نْ or one of the three tanween signs ً ٍ ٌ.
ruleSummary.result: Treat both as a noon sound when continuing, then inspect the immediately following letter.
ruleSummary.location: Noon saakinah can occur within or at the end of a word; tanween occurs at the end of a noun.

examplesHeading.title: Visual forms and reading examples
examplesHeading.subtitle: Identify what is written, then say what is heard when continuing.

quranExamples.readingInstruction: Pronounce noon with no added vowel.
quranExamples.teacherExplanation: The letter noon is visibly written and carries sukoon.

quranExamples.readingInstruction: When continuing, hear an an ending.
quranExamples.teacherExplanation: The doubled fathah represents tanween; there is no written noon.
quranExamples.commonError: Searching for a written ن in the ending.

quranExamples.readingInstruction: When continuing, hear an in ending.
quranExamples.teacherExplanation: The doubled kasrah represents tanween kasr.

quranExamples.readingInstruction: When continuing, hear an un ending.
quranExamples.teacherExplanation: The doubled dammah represents tanween damm.
quranExamples.commonError: Pronouncing only a single u sound when continuing.

commonMistakes: Confusing a single vowel sign with tanween.
Looking for a written noon inside tanween.
Adding a vowel after noon saakinah.
Inspecting the next letter before locating the target.
correctionTechniques: Use two columns: written noon versus heard noon sound.
Ask the learner to trace the actual letter ن.
Alternate isolated forms until recognition is automatic.
Repeat: find the target, then inspect the next letter.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: Name four randomly displayed target forms.
Give two differences between noon saakinah and tanween.
knowledgeChecks.success: Writing and position or stopping are mentioned.

teacherQuestions: What sound do you hear when continuing?
What comes after locating the target?
studentTasks: Sort forms into noon saakinah and tanween.
Explain one similarity and two differences.

liveClassFlow.display: Written noon versus additional noon sound

independentPractice: Write one line containing نْ and one containing each tanween form.
Label each form and say whether noon is written or heard.
homework: Find five teacher-approved targets containing noon saakinah or tanween.
Mark only the target; do not classify the four rules yet.
exitTicket: State: find the target, then inspect the next letter.
masteryCriteria: Recognizes نْ and all three tanween signs.
Explains the additional noon sound in tanween.
Distinguishes the forms in at least 8 of 10 items.
teacherNotes: Do not rush a learner who confuses the forms.
Keep rule names out of early recognition practice.
End by asking: What comes immediately after the target?
